## Week 1: Introduction & The Global Trade System

::: {.content-card}
### Day 1 — Monday, July 6: Introduction to IPE

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading 1:** Chapter 1 &middot; **Reading 2:** None (logistics day) &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day01.qmd) &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt &middot; Article presentation sign-up
:::

Course logistics and the foundations of IPE. We define the field, introduce the Open Economy Politics framework, walk through the three classical traditions (Smith, List, Marx), and trace globalization across four eras from 1815 to today.
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 2 — Tuesday, July 7: The WTO and World Trade System

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Chapter 2 &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day02.qmd) &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt
:::

From GATT to WTO: the evolution of multilateral trade institutions, dispute settlement, and contemporary challenges.
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 3 — Thursday, July 9: Political Economy of Trade Cooperation

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Ch. 3 + Bown &amp; Keynes (2020) &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day03.qmd) &middot; **Podcast:** [Trade Talks 17](https://tradetalkspodcast.com/podcast/17-wto-ministerials-now-and-then/) &middot; **In class:** Article presentation &middot; Writing prompt
:::

Why is international trade cooperation difficult to achieve? The role of institutions in facilitating cooperation.
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 4 — Friday, July 10: Society-Centered Trade Politics &middot; **Quiz 1**

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Ch. 4 + Carnegie &amp; Gaikwad (2022) &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day04.qmd) &middot; **Podcast:** [Trade Talks 198](https://tradetalkspodcast.com/podcast/198-inside-washingtons-lobbying-industry/) &middot; **In class:** Article presentation &middot; Quiz 1 (chapters 1–4)
:::

Domestic interest groups, factor endowments, and sectoral preferences in trade policy-making.
:::

## Week 2: Trade Politics & Development

::: {.content-card}
### Day 5 — Monday, July 13: State-Centered Trade Politics

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Ch. 5 + Bown &amp; Wang (2024) &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day05.qmd) &middot; **Podcast:** [Trade Talks 182](https://tradetalkspodcast.com/podcast/182-is-chinas-industrial-policy-working/) &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt
:::

National interests, state autonomy, and strategic trade policy. How governments balance domestic and international pressures.
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 6 — Tuesday, July 14: Trade and Development — ISI & Neoliberalism (combined)

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Chs. 6 & 7 + Irwin (2021) &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day06.qmd) &middot; **Podcast:** [Ideas of India](https://www.mercatus.org/ideasofindia/v-anantha-nageswaran-surveying-growth-and-financialization-indian-economy) &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt
:::

Two paired chapters: the logic and outcomes of import substitution industrialization (Ch 6), then the shift to neoliberal reforms — Washington Consensus, structural adjustment, and contemporary debates (Ch 7).
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 7 — Thursday, July 16: MNCs in the Global Economy

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Chapter 8 &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day07.qmd) &middot; **Podcast:** [Follow the Money (McKinsey)](https://www.mckinsey.com/mgi/our-research/follow-the-money-how-fdi-is-redrawing-the-global-economy) &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt
:::

What makes a firm multinational, and why produce abroad rather than trade or license? FDI and the modes of going global, the scale and shifting geography of investment, the OLI framework, horizontal vs. vertical FDI and global value chains, and the debate over whether FDI helps the countries that host it.
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 8 — Friday, July 17: The Politics of MNCs &middot; **Quiz 2**

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Ch. 9 + Bauerle Danzman (2025) &middot; **Slides:** [{{< fa laptop >}} View slides](day08.qmd) &middot; **Podcast:** [Economic Statecraft & FDI Screening (Skadden)](https://www.skadden.com/insights/podcasts/2025/03/economic-statecraft-and-foreign-investment-screening) &middot; **In class:** Article presentation &middot; Quiz 2 (chapters 5–9)
:::

How states try to govern multinationals: performance requirements, the Calvo Doctrine and expropriation, locational incentives and export-processing zones, and the obsolescing bargain. Why investment — unlike trade — has no "World Investment Organization," only a patchwork of treaties. We close on the emerging issue of national-security investment screening and CFIUS.
:::

## Week 4: International Finance & Synthesis

::: {.content-card}
### Day 13 — Monday, July 27: Debt, Capital Flows, and Crisis in the Developing World

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Chapters 14 & 15 (combined) &middot; **Slides:** Coming soon &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt
:::

A combined session on developing-country finance: capital flows and the 1980s Latin American debt crisis (Ch. 14), then the global capital-flow cycle and the 1990s emerging-market crises (Ch. 15). The IMF as crisis lender.
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 14 — Tuesday, July 28: Economic Coercion and Economic Statecraft

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Farrell & Newman (2019); Drezner (2024) &middot; **Slides:** [View slides](../slides/day14-economic-coercion.html){target="_blank"} &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt, discussion, and debate
:::

An instructor-led session outside the textbook: how states turn trade, money, and financial networks into instruments of coercion — export controls, the weaponized dollar, sanctions, and network chokepoints.
:::

::: {.content-card}
### Day 15 — Thursday, July 30: Achievements and Challenges of Global Capitalism

::: {.content-meta}
**Reading:** Chapter 16 &middot; **Slides:** [View slides](../slides/day15-chapter16.html){target="_blank"} &middot; **In class:** Writing prompt, student presentation
:::

Synthesizing the course: What has global capitalism achieved? What challenges does it face? Future trajectories.
:::

::: {.content-card}
